text:
GENERATE BURST K2c-gen-NW — Keeper H1 rest frame, direction NW — the base for the NW animation clips (Run C-3 P2, the 8-direction turnaround; S = master C). task_id "K2c-gen-NW".

Image 1 is the APPROVED IDENTITY MASTER (direction S, facing the camera) — identity, face, hair, costume, colours, proportions and painted register come ONLY from Image 1. Image 2 is a GEOMETRY-ONLY reference: an earlier, differently-drawn version of the same character type already turned to NW — copy from it ONLY the body turn and which side each item lands on; do NOT copy its face, hair, proportions, brushwork, colours or register.

Deliver EXACTLY ONE image: the SAME character as Image 1, turned to direction NW: a BACK three-quarter view — she faces the viewer's UPPER-LEFT, turned 135° from the S pose, walking away from the camera toward screen-left. Her BACK and her LEFT side are visible; her LEFT side is nearer the camera: the olive satchel hangs AT HER SIDE on her near LEFT hip, on the SCREEN-LEFT, nearest the camera; the strap crosses her BACK diagonally from her far RIGHT shoulder (screen-right) down to that satchel. Her RIGHT arm holds the staff upright on the FAR side, on the SCREEN-RIGHT, behind her, the staff tip above her far shoulder. Her head is turned AWAY toward the upper-left — the face is NOT visible (at most the edge of a cheek and an ear), the tied-back curly hair visible; head level.

The camera is fixed for every direction: an elevated three-quarter pinhole view from the front, ~53° above the ground plane (projection C); the character turns, the camera does not. The light is fixed for every direction: a single key from SCREEN UPPER-LEFT that does NOT rotate with the character — the key-facing side is the screen-left side in every direction; deep cool ambient; readable shadows, never pure black; slight rim on the key-facing edge; no spell glow; NO floor shadow. NO MIRRORING: this is the character turned, never a flipped image — the staff stays in the ANATOMICAL RIGHT hand, the satchel on the ANATOMICAL LEFT hip, the strap over the RIGHT shoulder, whichever side those land on screen. Same framing and standing height as Image 1: full body, feet fully visible, centred, standing rest pose (weight even, arms relaxed, the staff upright), on a flat uniform pure #00ff00 background covering the whole canvas; portrait canvas like Image 1 (1024×1536); do not matte. Identity, unchanged from Image 1: a YOUNG WOMAN, early 20s, dark curly hair tied back, sun-browned; ivory linen shirt with rolled sleeves, navy sleeveless tabard with a PLAIN chest and back (no emblem of any kind), ONE chestnut diagonal harness strap carrying an olive canvas satchel with brass corners on her LEFT hip, ONE waist belt with a brass buckle, chestnut laced bracers, navy trousers, chestnut buckled boots; a PLAIN dark walnut staff with small brass ferrules at foot and tip (NO ring, NO head-piece) in the RIGHT hand; NO insignia anywhere — every surface plain. Register: HAND-DRAWN painted 2D in the manner of a modern hand-animated action game — a confident dark contour line drawn by hand with visible taper and varying weight, painted fills in clean planes inside the line, restrained texture; the line carries the pose. It should look like one frame of hand-drawn animation, not a rendered illustration.

One image_gen call; ONE retry only if the result is off-plate, has a baked checkerboard, is mirrored (the staff in the wrong anatomical hand, or the satchel on the wrong hip), faces the wrong way, or invents extra objects — name the retry reason in the receipt. Copy the final output from $CODEX_HOME/generated_images/... to out/k2c_NW.png and compute its sha256. No code. No other files. No web. No agents.
RETURN: the receipt (task_id "K2c-gen-NW"): images = the one file with prompt, references (role + path), elapsed_s; calls_used = the TRUE number of image_gen calls (1 or 2); status DELIVERED / DELIVERED_WITH_CONCERNS / FAILED; concerns naming anything you could not honour. Never PASS/FAIL.

GEOMETRY-ONLY reference for the NW view (body turn + item sides) — do NOT copy its face, register or brushwork
